Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why didn't Sidious turn younglings into inquisitors?
Answer: He did, but first he sadistically made them fight each other to the death,..before the winner reluctantly joined the Inquisitorious under the oversight of Sidious himself. This was the cruel Sith Lord postulating over his victory over the Jedi, and rounding up the survivors of Order 66 and the Great Purge. Palpatine would have the survivors starved and beaten, then bought before him. Then he would make them fight to the death, with the victor being promised freedom. It's not that Sidious ever intended for the young Jedi to become Inquisitors, but if they survived his punishment and killed their fellow Jedi they stood a good chance of becoming one of his agents. He did this to a group of young survivors and ‘persuaded’ a Verpine Jedi named Beyghor Sadhett to turn on his Jedi brothers and sisters. This didn't mean that he was instantly to become an Inquisitor at all,..because he was later killed by Vader. Sadhett died because when he first met Vader he immediately assumed that the two of them were equals or allies on the same team. Vader took immense displease at the Verpines unsolicited insolence. Less than one percent of the entire Jedi Order survived the purge, making that just less than 100 Jedi left on the run. Of the remaining Jedi far more survivors would have been adults than younglings, and it was easier for Palpatine to use seasoned adult fighters than children in his army of Jedi Assassins. The younglings in the Temple were a test for Vader orchestrated by Sidious..to test his conscience and morals, and ensure his descent into the darkside was cemented. Sadly these younglings were just fodder for Vaders initiation, and nothing more. Reva Sevander was a youngling that actually survived the Purge by playing dead, but then it's hazy on how she actually came to join the Inquisitorious afterwards. Eeth Koths infant son was immediately taken by Vader and his Inquisitors after crossing the Jedi off their hit list. But the majority of the younglings from the Temple were slaughtered, and those that survived either quickly went into hiding like Grogu, or were swiftly hunted down. Sidious wanted to be done with the Jedi Order for good and didn't want to take forever achieving it. A youngling survivor could be a serious threat further down the road, like Sevander proved to be, so the Emperor had the unfortunates immediately dealt with. Younglings could integrate easier into a large society, and have a family smuggle them.. whereas older Jedi had more risks of being detected. Sidious was meticulous with his ages old plan, and the younglings had their purpose to serve after he began sweeping away the Jedi.

Question: Does Jabba the Hutt realize that Darth Vader is Anakin Skywalker, the little boy who won the pod race?
Answer: Jabba the Hutt probably wouldn't have remembered who won a pod race more than 30 years prior to when he met Luke Skywalker, and he most definitely would have kept this secret from Jabba at all costs. There's nothing to suggest that the Hutt knew Anakin Skywalker was the second most powerful being in the galaxy, despite the fact that Vader once rescued his son Rotta during the Clone Wars. Rotta was kidnapped by Dooku in a bid to destabilise relationships between the Republic and the Hutts, but Anakin and Ahsoka were tasked with returning the 55 year old infant back to his crimelord father. During the reign of the Empire Jabba became aware that Luke was Vaders son, meanwhile he was completely unaware that Vader was once the great Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker. It's uncertain if Jabba remembered little Anakin Skywalker, when years later he became a Jedi and saved his son, but then again if Jabba knew Darth Vaders identity I don't think he'd be foolish enough to let the Sith Lord know. You might assume that Jabba may have used this juicy information as leverage against Vader, but the Hutt didn't control Tatooine by being headstrong and stupid. When Jabba eventually learned that Luke was Vaders son the Hutt was genuinely suprised that anyone of decent reputation was ever born on Tatooine, suggesting that he had no clue about Vader,…and his strong, very familiar ties to the desert planet. But I'm guessing that if Jabba knew how he was going to die he would have killed Skywalker immediately after rescuing Rotta.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if Count Dooku betrayed Darth Sidious?
Answer: Then he better bring some help with him, because if he faces Darth Sidious alone then he will probably be defeated. Darth Sidious faced both Maul and Savage on Mandalore. He killed Savage and actually captured his former apprentice Maul. During the epic duel Darth Sidious didn't even break a sweat, and was grinning sadistically the whole time. This was no contest for the dark lord of the Sith, and we must remember that Dooku was trained extensively by Palpatine. Sure, Dooku was one of the most skilled swordsman when he was a Jedi, and even more refined and ferocious when he became a Sith. But Sidious didn't even need his lightsabers, and almost every other opponent he faced was met with a barrage of devastating force lightning. Dooku was force choked by his own apprentice, Savage, and subsequently fled from said confrontation. If he couldn't defeat Savage then I don't like his chances with Sidious. With Dooku defeated all that Darth Sidious loses is time. Dooku was going to be replaced by Anakin Skywalker, this is a given because Sidious had his sights set on ‘The Chosen One’ even when Skywalker was a padawan. Dooku was always going to be supplanted by a younger, stronger apprentice, and later Sidious even tells this to Vader. Dooku was viewed as a proton torpedo, that served his purpose and was gone. Until Skywalker is turned to the darkside Palpatine would have to do without the Count, and more than likely replace him within the Separatist Alliance until the Clone Wars ceased. Grievous could fill this role, but within the Separatist Senate someone with a more diplomatic touch would be required to keep the Confederacy of Independent Systems in line. Either way as I said before, the only thing that Darth Sidious is going to lose is time, with the Clone Wars being stretched out just a little further. In time Skywalker would be his to control, regardless.

Question: How did Imperials on Coruscant and other core worlds react to the destruction of the Death Star?
Answer: Just ask the Imperial pilot that Cara Dune shot in the face. The destruction of the Death Star, and it's predecessor years later, reverberated for many years throughout the Star Wars Universe…and had a very profound affect on those Imperials serving under Palpatines yoke during the reign of his Empire. Darth Vader was the sole survivor of the destruction of the first Death Star, and his survival meant only to boost dwindling morale for the remaining Imperials throughout the galaxy. For the Emperors mightiest superweapon to be destroyed by a teenager from Tatooine was the Empires single largest loss since it's formation nearly two decades prior. The Death Stars destruction was such a significant intergalactic event within the SWU that dates are measured from before, and after, the Battle of Yavin…where Galen Ersos subterfuge led to the destruction of the galaxy's most powerful weapon. The Death Star was a symbol of ultimate power for the Empire, and it's supporters, and with its destruction was felt a terrible vacuum of power;..but only for a short time, before the unleashing of the Death Stars first reincarnation above Endors moon. The Death Star was a means of controlling the entire galaxy, but some high ranking Imperial officers thought that Palpatine hedging all his bets into one superweapon was ill advised. And so Lukes shot hit no-one harder than Palpatine himself. In one blast by a lone X-Wing pilot Palps’ grand plan was blown to pieces in the blink of an eye. He looked weak in the minds of the citizens under his control, and his supporters had very real cause for concern. Until the fully functional Death Star II was ready to rock Palpatine and his Imperials reacted very, very negatively to their failure over Yavin. Vader personally felt Palpatines wrath and fury over his failure to protect their greatest asset. This was a monumental set back for every Imperial, and it was safe to say that they were infuriated, at the least. Their moment of triumph became their greatest failure in a heartbeat. Resentment for years was felt within the Imperial community, and after the destruction of the second Death Star it only spurned some Imperials to harbor even more resentment towards the Rebel Alliance and their terrorist co-conspirators. This is witnessed during season 2, episode 8, of The Mandalorian, where operatives of the New Republic attack Imperial remnants led by Moff Gideon. During an Imperial shuttle hijack, led by Marshal Cara Dune, we hear first hand from an Imperial pilot on his thoughts about the destruction of the Death Star. He bitterly resented the actions of the Rebel Alliance that fateful day years earlier, and it strengthened his hatred towards all enemies of the Empire. He even shot his copilot in the back for not being loyal to the Empire. He condemned the loss of millions of lives aboard both battle stations, and viewed the destruction of Alderaan as a ‘small price to pay’ to rid the galaxy of terrorism. He was actually aboard the Death Star when it obliterated its first planet. Like every diehard Imperial this pilot viewed the destruction of both Death Stars as an act of galactic terrorism, condemning the millions of lives lost at the hands of Rebel criminals. Unfortunately this didn't stop Marshal Dune from shooting him in the face, for taunting her about the obliteration of her homeworld,..Alderaan.

Question: What changed between Kenobi's 1st and 2nd confrontation with Maul and Savage in terms of his ability? In the first one he claims that Ventress and he are outmatched, in the second he wins confidently on his own.
Answer: When Kenobi first fought both Maul and Savage, in the aftermath of the Massacre on Raydonia, he was caught off guard a little. The last time he had seen Maul was when he bisected him on Naboo,..and had actually thought he was dead; until Maul himself contacted the Jedi Council.. and executed civilian hostages on Raydonia in a bid to lure Kenobi on his own terms. Kenobi arrives, playing straight into the Dathomiri brothers trap, and after witnessing an entire village ablaze..and its citizens murdered..Kenobi is initially stunned a bit at Mauls sudden appearance, and his brother Savage backing him up. This was his first encounter with both the Nightbrothers together, and he learned much from this first and failed fight. He was being ragdolled by the brothers until Ventress saved the day, but nonetheless escaped and evaluated himself against the pair. Ventress was capable of choking two Jedi’s simultaneously, and had tutored under Count Dooku, so she actually evened the odds slightly..despite Kenobis protest to being out matched. They were ultimately out matched, but managed to turn the tables on the brothers in the long run. But it wasn't sheer skill and tactics that led him to defeat Maul and Savage on Florrum. In his second encounter with the horned crazies Kenobi was accompanied by another Jedi Master, Adi Gallia. He had learned from the previous encounter not to be too hasty, but Gallia was no match for Savages ferocity. After retreating, and again assessing his odds, he uses Pirate leader Hondo Ohnaka and his reformed gang, to assist him. Leading the pair away to a more secluded area he skillfully attacks in the same spot on Savages leg, like Gallia did, and lands a critical blow. This enables him to sever Savages arm and completely disrupt the fight. He also used Gallias lightsaber to fight in a more aggressive defence style. This enabled him to keep both attackers at bay more, and calculate counter strikes. The brothers only chance at victory was to now retreat themselves, which Kenobi had forced them into..much like they'd done to him on Raydonia. Somehow I also think that the death of Gallia spurned Kenobi into greatness, much like we witnessed him do much later on Mustafar, after the death of the Jedi Order. Kenobis resolve was incredible, which led him to his abilities being enhanced under great pressure.
